description: Reference identity-ladder derivation. `input` is the exact value map handed to the ladder walker; `expected.raw` is the full result object (or null when no rung fires). `expected.rung` identifies the producing rung by its 0-based index in `ladders[slug].rungs`. `validates` is the full canonical-form validation of the derived IID (a rung may produce an IID that fails it, e.g. a URL over the 220-character value cap); `classificationWrapperThrows` records the classification-level wrapper that rejects such IIDs. The wd scheme only mints when the rung declares an ACTIVE typed slug; untyped and dormant wd rungs are skipped by the walker, so their evidence falls through to lower rungs (observable in the `wd` cases).

book.identifies: the work; isbn identifies editions, bridged via equivalence

brand.identifies: a brand/concept (instance businesses are local-business atoms)

comment.identifies: one comment on one subject (relational entity)

dataset.identifies: a dataset (version lineage out of ID scope)

defined-term.identifies: a term within a term set

ethereum-erc20.identifies: a token asset on a chain

image.identifies: an image — byte-identity first; url is a mutable manifestation fallback

local-business.identifies: one business at one place (instance level)

location.identifies: a named place or coordinate point

mobile-application.identifies: a mobile app per store ecosystem

music-album.identifies: the release-group (the album as a work)

music-recording.identifies: the recording (isrc level; compositions are iswc territory)

podcast-episode.identifies: one FEED ITEM (manifestation) — the episode-work is the equivalence cluster over feed items

review.identifies: one review of one subject (relational entity)

social-media-account.identifies: an account on a platform (the person behind it is a separate atom)

software.identifies: the package/project, version-free — purl (open spec) first; repo URLs migrate

thing.identifies: anything not covered by a specific classification (weakest IDs by design)

video-object.identifies: a video — byte-identity first; platform URLs are manifestation fallbacks

web-page.identifies: a page at a canonical URL
